QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_45

question.text: At expiry, in-the-money stock options are:

answer.text: Automatically exercised on expiry day and settled by physical delivery
Automatically lapsed if not explicitly exercised by the holder
Settled in cash without any exercise action needed
Rolled over to the next expiry automatically

explanation.text: The Logic: All in-the-money stock option contracts are automatically exercised on expiry day, and stock options are settled by physical delivery of the underlying shares — the short side delivers and the long side takes delivery and pays the settlement amount. The Trap: ITM options do NOT lapse — they are auto-exercised. There is no automatic rollover into the next expiry. And because stock options settle by physical delivery, the long ITM holder ends up with shares (or has to deliver them, if a short call writer), not just a cash payout. Note: Cash settlement applies to index options, not to stock options. Stock option ITM positions become deliverable positions at expiry.
